chunks: Or, lest they should say: 'It were our fathers who had ascribed compeers to God; we are only their offspring. Will You destroy us for the deeds of those who dealt in vanities?'
ai.seo_question: What is the argument of the polytheists' descendants on the Day of Judgment regarding their fathers' sins?
ai.summary: In this verse, the polytheists' descendants attempt to shift blame to their ancestors, arguing that inherited sin should absolve them of personal accountability. Shia scholars, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, emphasize that this rhetorical question highlights the principle of *'Adl* (Divine Justice), where God does not punish the innocent for the sins of the guilty, yet individual responsibility remains paramount. The verse serves as a counter-argument to the idea of generational guilt, reinforcing that each soul bears its own burden.
